style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The last of the 'the LORD reigns' psalms, and the one that says what the reign is made of: holiness. Three times -- at verses 3, 5, and 9 -- the refrain comes: 'He is holy' twice, and then, with the full Name, 'the LORD our God is holy' -- the seraphim's threefold cry of Isaiah 6 spread across a psalm. The King sits enthroned on the cherubim, great in Zion and high over all the peoples, and the earth is told to stagger; but His strength is in love with justice, and He has actually done justice and righteousness in Jacob. Then the psalm names three men who proved the holy King can be approached: Moses and Aaron among His priests, Samuel among those who called on His name -- they called, and He answered, from the pillar of cloud, and they kept what He gave them. The eighth verse holds the tension of Exodus 34 without resolving it: You were a forgiving God to them, and You took vengeance on their deeds. Worship is commanded at two places -- His footstool, and His holy hill -- because the infinite King has a place where His feet touch the earth, and that is where His people put their faces.

1.text: The LORD reigns; let the peoples shake with fear! He is enthroned upon the cherubim; let the earth stagger under Him.
1.amp: The LORD [YHWH] reigns [malak]; let the people [am] tremble [ragaz]: He sits [yashab] between the cherubims [kerub]; let the earth [eretz] be moved ['stagger', nut, the KJV margin].
1.notes: YHWH malakh yirgezu ammim (H4427, H7264, H5971): the third psalm to open with 'the LORD reigns' (93, 97, 99; the cry also sounds mid-psalm at 96:10), and this time the peoples are told to tremble, not cheer -- yoshev kerubim (H3427, H3742): enthroned on the cherubim, with the ark beneath as His footstool (cf. 1 Samuel 4:4). tanut ha-aretz (H5120, H776): let the earth stagger, the margin's word. A holiness psalm: the refrain will come three times.

2.text: The LORD is great in Zion; He is high above all the peoples.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is great [gadol] in Zion [Tsiyyon]; and He is high [rum] above all the people [am].
2.notes: YHWH be-Tsiyyon gadol (H3068, H6726, H1419): great IN Zion -- the universal King has a local address -- ve-ram hu al-kol-ha-ammim (H7311, H5971): and high over all the peoples. The particular and the universal in one verse, as in Psalm 48:1-2 (great in the city of our God, and the joy of the whole earth); the 'high above all nations' half is Psalm 113:4.

3.text: Let them give thanks to Your great and awesome name -- He is holy!
3.amp: Let them praise [yadah] Your great [gadol] and terrible [yare -- awesome, fearful] name [shem]; for it is holy ['he is holy', qadosh].
3.notes: yodu shimkha gadol ve-nora (H3034, H8034, H1419, H3372): the Name great and awe-inspiring -- qadosh hu (H6918): HOLY is He -- the first of three refrains (vv. 3, 5, 9), the threefold 'holy' of Isaiah 6:3 spread across a psalm. Holiness is the theme the enthronement psalms have been building toward.

4.text: The King's strength loves justice; You have established equity; You have done justice and righteousness in Jacob.
4.amp: The King's [melek] strength [oz] also loves [ahab] judgment [mishpat -- justice]; You do establish [kun] equity [meyshar -- straightness]; You execute [asah] judgment [mishpat] and righteousness [tsedaqah] in Jacob [Yaaqob].
4.notes: ve-oz melekh mishpat ahev (H5797, H4428, H4941, H157): the King's STRENGTH loves justice -- power that is in love with fairness, the rarest thing in politics. attah konanta mesharim (H3559, H4339): You set up straightness; mishpat u-tsedaqah be-Yaaqob attah asita (H6666, H3290, H6213): justice and righteousness DONE in Jacob, not merely decreed.

5.text: Exalt the LORD our God, and bow down at His footstool -- He is holy!
5.amp: Exalt [rum] ye the LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim], and worship [shachah -- bow down] at His footstool [hadom regel]; for He is holy ['it is holy', qadosh, the KJV margin].
5.notes: romemu YHWH Elohenu (H7311, H3068, H430): lift Him high -- ve-hishtachavu la-hadom raglav (H7812, H1916, H7272): bow at the footstool of His feet, the ark (cf. 1 Chronicles 28:2) -- qadosh hu (H6918): the second refrain. The footstool is the point where the infinite King's feet touch the earth; that is where the worshipers put their faces.

6.text: Moses and Aaron were among His priests, and Samuel among those who call on His name; they called to the LORD, and He answered them.
6.amp: Moses [Mosheh] and Aaron [Aharon] among His priests [kohen], and Samuel [Shemuel] among them that call [qara] upon His name [shem]; they called upon the LORD [YHWH], and He answered [anah] them.
6.notes: Mosheh ve-Aharon be-khohanav (H4872, H175, H3548): Moses and Aaron among His priests; u-Shemuel be-qorei shemo (H8050, H7121, H8034): Samuel among those calling on His name -- three intercessors: Moses at Sinai, Aaron with the censer, Samuel at Mizpah (cf. 1 Samuel 7:9) -- qorim el-YHWH ve-hu yaanem (H6030): they called and He answered. The holy King is approachable by prayer; that is the psalm's second theme.

7.text: He spoke to them from within the pillar of cloud; they kept the testimonies He gave, and the statute He set for them.
7.amp: He spoke [dabar] unto them in the cloudy [anan] pillar [ammud]: they kept [shamar] His testimonies [edah], and the ordinance [choq -- statute] that He gave [natan] them.
7.notes: be-ammud anan yedabber alehem (H5982, H6051, H1696): the pillar of cloud as a pulpit -- Exodus 33:9 -- shameru edotav ve-choq natan-lamo (H8104, H5713, H2706, H5414): they KEPT the testimonies. Answered prayer and kept commandments in the same breath: the intercessors were also obeyers.

8.text: You answered them, O LORD our God; You were a God who lifted their guilt away, yet one who took vengeance on their misdeeds.
8.amp: You answered [anah] them, O LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim]: You were a God [El] that forgave [nasa -- lifted, carried away] them, though You took vengeance [naqam] of their inventions [alilah -- their doings, their deeds].
8.notes: YHWH Elohenu attah anitam (H6030): You answered THEM -- El nose hayita lahem (H410, H5375): a lifting-God, the nasa of Psalm 32:1 -- ve-noqem al-alilotam (H5358, H5949): AND avenging their deeds -- whether the intercessors' own (Moses and Aaron barred from the land, Numbers 20:12) or, as many read it, the people's they prayed for (pardoned at the calf yet plagued, Exodus 32:35; pardoned at Kadesh yet barred, Numbers 14:20-23). Forgiveness and discipline in one God, one verse -- Exodus 34:7's tension held, not resolved.

9.text: Exalt the LORD our God, and bow down at His holy hill -- for the LORD our God is holy!
9.amp: Exalt [rum] the LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim], and worship [shachah] at His holy [qodesh] hill [har]; for the LORD our God is holy [qadosh].
9.notes: romemu YHWH Elohenu ve-hishtachavu le-har qodsho (H7311, H7812, H2022, H6944): verse 5 again, the footstool widened to the whole holy hill -- ki-qadosh YHWH Elohenu (H6918): the third refrain, now with the full Name: holy is the LORD our God. The thrice-holy complete; Isaiah's seraphim and the Psalter's congregation singing the same word.
